summary: Produced the four sourced Revit knowledge-base references for the revit-bridge skill (revit-import-fidelity.md, mep-class-map.md, shared-parameters-mapping.md, revit-versions.md, ~11.5k words total, TL;DR + details + Sources in each), grounded primarily in a code read of Autodesk's open-source Link-IFC importer (vendor/revit-ifc, already cloned, commit f534ad1) plus Autodesk help/IFC Manual/APS docs, with every claim tagged [src]/[docs]/[forum]/[unverified]. Key verdicts: Link IFC turns every IfcProduct into a DirectShape (both the legacy and 2024.1+ AnyCAD engines); Open IFC is a separate closed engine limited to IFC2x3 that we should never recommend; the importer contains zero connector/circuit creation (ports become cone-arrow DirectShapes) — the MEP answer is a hard no; psets auto-become bound shared parameters named PsetName.PropertyName with importer GUIDs, and a source-derived pre-seeded sidecar technique can make them adopt the firm's GUIDs. Out-of-scope findings dropped in docs/inbox/revit-fidelity.md.
key_findings: Three routes, two engines: Link IFC (Intent=Reference) runs the open-source importer (+ AnyCAD hybrid since 2024.1, revit.ini [ImportIFC] LinkProcessor=Default|Legacy|AnyCAD) and produces an intermediate <name>.ifc.RVT of DirectShapes plus .ifc.log.html and .ifc.sharedparameters.txt; Open IFC (Intent=Parametric) is a closed internal engine limited to IFC2x3/2x2/2x that posts a partial-schema warning for IFC4 and cannot open IFC4.3; Insert>Import CAD does not accept IFC.

MEP truth (source-verified, exhaustive grep = 0 connector/circuit API calls): Revit's importer never creates connectors, ElectricalSystems, circuits or panel schedules; an IfcDistributionPort becomes its own Generic Model DirectShape with a point + revolved cone arrow and text params (Flow Direction, System Type, IfcPort ConnectedTo/From GUID/Name), IfcDistributionSystem becomes a container DirectShape with SystemClassification/SystemName strings; corroborated by Autodesk (Angel Velez) statements.

Geometry fidelity ladder inside the DirectShape: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid/revolved/swept -> real Revit Solid; Brep -> Solid if watertight; IfcTriangulatedFaceSet -> Solid only if closed else Mesh (our v1 = 100% facesets = worst tier); IfcMappedItem with uniform transform -> real instancing (RepresentationMap becomes a shape-library DirectShapeType, occurrences are GeometryInstances); ObjectPlacement is baked into geometry (ApplyTransforms=true) so DirectShapes have no insertion point/rotation; IfcTypeObject -> DirectShapeType; IfcBuildingStorey -> real Level; IfcSpace -> Generic Models (never a Revit Room); GlobalId (IFC_GUID param) is the reload match key.

Psets -> parameters: every IfcPropertySet property becomes an instance shared parameter (ExternalDefinition in the auto-written <name>.ifc.sharedparameters.txt, groups 'IFC Parameters'/'IFC Type Parameters', bound to the category, group IFC), named PsetName.PropertyName (' Type' suffix for type psets), typed from the IFC measure (IfcElectricVoltageMeasure -> Electrical Potential, IfcLabel -> Text) — so exporting Voltage as a labelled string permanently breaks typing; there is NO import-side parameter mapping table.

Route B technique (derived from source, needs one live test): because the importer reuses an existing definition found by exact name inside an existing sidecar file, pre-seeding <name>.ifc.sharedparameters.txt with the firm's GUIDs under names like PanelSchedule.PanelName makes the imported parameters carry the firm's parameter identities, so existing tags/schedules resolve; Route A (schedule the Pset-prefixed params with 'Include elements in links') always works.

Class->category map for our domain (built-in, from IFCCategoryUtil): IfcElectricDistributionBoard/IfcTransformer -> Electrical Equipment; IfcLightFixture -> Lighting Fixtures; IfcOutletType POWEROUTLET/IfcSwitchingDevice/IfcJunctionBox -> Electrical Fixtures; IfcDiscreteAccessory -> Specialty Equipment; IfcCableCarrierSegment (even CONDUITSEGMENT) -> Cable Trays, Conduits fed only by IfcCableSegment; IfcElectricGenerator/IfcElectricFlowStorageDevice/IfcElectricMotor and untyped IfcOutlet are unmapped -> Generic Models with a log warning (no supertype fallback) — fixable by shipping a complete importIFCClassMapping.txt, which the Link code does read (Application.ImportIFCCategoryTable) despite the manual saying otherwise.

Version rules: .rvt files never open in older Revit and cannot be saved down (Autodesk KB); file version is readable from BasicFileInfo ('F o r m a t' in Notepad) which our rvt tooling already parses; IFC is version-agnostic and the .ifc.RVT is created by the user's own Revit; IFC4 import is Link-only in all releases 2023-2026, IFC4.3 link experimental in 2023.1/2024 and supported from 2025; the IFC add-in updates independently of Revit; Design Automation lets us choose the Revit engine year, solving version targeting for any generated .rvt.

Validators: Autodesk Viewer web is free and accepts both IFC and RVT (Revit 2015+) — proves parse/translate/geometry only, not Revit categories or parameters; APS Model Derivative is a rated API since the 2025-12-08 business model (0.5 token per complex job, RVT/IFC = complex, free monthly tier) but exact free allowance and USD token price could not be verified from the pricing page and are flagged; Revit itself is only free via the 30-day full trial or read-only viewer mode (save/export blocked; Link IFC in viewer mode unverified).
